title: A lifecycle document
description: An organization's lifecycle, kept as a file: which of the stages in stages.json it uses, who holds each role, and the stages it adds of its own, for the organization and for each project. A project's choices override the organization's, stage by stage and role by role. Anything not chosen follows the default: every stage used, and each role held by its reference agent. No service is needed to read or write it.

organization.description: The organization's choices. Every build follows them unless its project chose otherwise.

projects.description: Each project's choices, by project name.

used.description: Whether each stage is used, by stage id: false leaves it out, true uses it. A stage not listed follows the wider scope, or the default, which uses it.

holders.description: Who holds each role, by role id. A role not listed follows the wider scope, or the default, its reference agent.

added_stages.description: Stages of this scope's own, each placed after a stage.

approvers.description: Who may answer each stage's person gate, by stage id: people and teams, as the organization's list of people names them. A stage listed here replaces the wider scope's list for that stage. Anyone may answer a gate whose stage is listed nowhere. Optional.

Approver.description: One person, by email, or one team, by name: exactly one of the two.

handle.description: Its handle on the mesh. A your_agent or contracted holder has one.

settings.description: The holder's settings for this role, as the holder reads them: any JSON object, such as how often a watcher checks or the most a product may spend. A service keeps them with the build and hands them to the holder unchanged. A role that holds more than one stage, such as the watcher holding Monitor and Cost, may keep each stage's settings under that stage's id, such as { "monitor": { "every_minutes": 5 }, "cost": { "monthly_ceiling": 50 } } (lifecycle API 0.4.4). Never a key or other secret value.

id.description: Unique among every stage, including those in stages.json.

phase.description: A phase id from stages.json, such as "make".

after.description: The stage it comes after, in the same phase; null puts it first in its phase.

role.description: A role id from stages.json, or a new role this document names.

role_name.description: The new role's name. Present only when role is not in stages.json.

person_gate.description: Whether a person must say yes before the stage is done.
